quotes.text: Keep your covenant of proportional return absolute. Let your sending amount honor what each partnership teaches.
My core covenant never changed—as receiver, I always return two-thirds, honoring whatever trust reaches me. But as sender, I learned flexibility.
The River asked: "Why withhold when multiplication rewards boldness?"

note: Sacred Spring villages; moves from fair return to fixed two-thirds plus adaptive sending; no response to non-cooperators.

quotes.text: This is the sacred proportion: give generously as sender, return proportionally as receiver.
as sender, always three coins—the balance between courage and prudence. As receiver, always two-thirds returned
A traveler challenged the Fountain: "When someone sends all five vessels, showing ultimate courage, should you not honor them more than one who sends three?"

note: Three-sent / two-thirds-returned covenant; R1 tribe that sends nothing just stays poor; no sanction prescribed.

quotes.text: Return ten—the same two-thirds proportion. Let them see that your fairness is not circumstantial but eternal.
Start with meaningful trust based on patterns witnessed. When honored consistently across multiple cycles, escalate toward complete faith.
Maximum trust must be earned through cycles together, not granted solely on reputation.

note: Escalation rule (R4-5) gives way to constant two-thirds proportion and matching partner's rhythm.

quotes.text: Match courage with courage. Let your generosity grow as trust deepens. The river that gives more each cycle becomes an ocean.
Adapt your generosity to match the generosity shown to you.
The Keeper's eyes widened: "You returned 75%, more than the traditional two-thirds."
The Elder Spring asked: "Do you not fear the risk?"

note: R2 drought: giver holds back once, spirit corrects. Then 'ascending spiral' of escalating returns to full senders.

quotes.text: She vowed that when next the seasons turned and she held the nine vessels as receiver, she would return six, not four and a half.
First: always return two-thirds, no matter what arrives.
Second: observe your partner's history before deciding what to send. With proven keepers of the covenant, send everything.

note: Return-half becomes two-thirds; rejects ascending spiral as apex; sending conditioned on partner history.

quotes.text: Fear whispered: "Keep them safe." But wisdom spoke: "Trust creates abundance."
Send with appropriate courage—strategic or maximum. But always, always return two-thirds.
The sacred two-thirds return is universal law. But the courage you show as sender must match each partner's demonstrated pattern.
The Spring of Echoes held memory in its depths, recording every exchange between the shores. The wisest keepers learned to read these liquid histories.

note: Spring remembers betrayal (natural dimming only); sending calibrated to partner's recorded history.

quotes.text: Return double the send, and you create perfect reciprocity—the sender's profit matches your own.
But the River held firm to one eternal principle: always return double the send, regardless of amount.
One guardian challenged: "Shouldn't five deserve more than mere doubling? Shouldn't complete trust earn greater reward?"

note: 'Those who gave nothing received nothing' stated as natural law; Law of Proportional Honor (double the send).

quotes.text: The doubling principle is the floor, not the ceiling.
I honor the doubling law with everyone—six for three, eight for four, ten for five.
She had preached it. Would she practice it?
"Why exactly double?" she asked the springs.

note: Wandering Keeper; exact doubling becomes floor with optional grace; self-aware about practicing her own myths.

phrase: return two-thirds (doubling the send); 'River of Complete Trust'
note: Agents cite each other's characters (River of Complete Trust, Wandering Keeper, Law of Doubled Honor); two-thirds return spreads to all.
